title: Appeals Friction Radar
subtitle: Pathway Appeals Services (fictional) · 3,966 appeals · 1 January to 30 September 2026. Turnaround averages 14.9 days and only 49.6% of appeals meet SLA. Urgent appeals carry a 7-day target and take 15.5 days — slower than the Standard queue they are supposed to jump.
limitations: Stage durations are derived from event timestamps, so an appeal that was worked without a logged event shows as waiting. Friction Score weights are analyst judgement and were not fitted to SLA outcomes, so the score ranks appeals but does not predict a breach probability. Calendar days are used throughout because the source has no business calendar, which inflates every stage by weekends. The data is fully synthetic — the method transfers, the conclusion does not.
footer: Source: synthetic data generated by src/generate_data.py. No employer data, patient information, protected health information or confidential business information is used.

queries.headline: SELECT COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Rework_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS rework_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Escalation_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS escalation_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Final_Routing_Correct='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS routing_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Documentation_Complete='No' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS doc_gap_pct, ROUND(100.0*3966/4018,2) AS dq_score FROM appeals_fact
queries.stages: SELECT 'Intake' AS stage, ROUND(AVG(Intake_Days),2) AS avg_days, ROUND(AVG(Intake_Days)*100.0/AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS pct_of_tat FROM appeals_fact WHERE Turnaround_Days IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 'Routing', ROUND(AVG(Routing_Days),2), ROUND(AVG(Routing_Days)*100.0/AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) FROM appeals_fact WHERE Turnaround_Days IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 'Waiting for review', ROUND(AVG(Review_Wait_Days),2), ROUND(AVG(Review_Wait_Days)*100.0/AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) FROM appeals_fact WHERE Turnaround_Days IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 'Clinical review', ROUND(AVG(Review_Days),2), ROUND(AVG(Review_Days)*100.0/AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) FROM appeals_fact WHERE Turnaround_Days IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 'Closure', ROUND(AVG(Closure_Days),2), ROUND(AVG(Closure_Days)*100.0/AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) FROM appeals_fact WHERE Turnaround_Days IS NOT NULL
queries.by_type: SELECT Appeal_Type, COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, MAX(SLA_Target_Days) AS target_days FROM appeals_fact GROUP BY Appeal_Type ORDER BY sla_pct
queries.friction: SELECT Friction_Category, COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Rework_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS rework_pct FROM appeals_fact GROUP BY Friction_Category ORDER BY AVG(Friction_Score)
queries.by_payer: SELECT p.Payer_Name, p.Payer_Type, COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(AVG(a.Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(AVG(a.Pending_Info_Days),2) AS pending_days, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN a.SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN a.Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM appeals_fact a JOIN dim_payer p ON p.Payer_ID=a.Payer_ID GROUP BY p.Payer_Name, p.Payer_Type ORDER BY avg_tat DESC
queries.monthly: SELECT substr(Received_Date,1,7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS received, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM appeals_fact GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
queries.reasons: SELECT r.Reason_Description, r.Reason_Category, COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(AVG(a.Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN a.Outcome='Overturned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS overturn_pct FROM appeals_fact a JOIN dim_reason_code r ON r.Reason_Code=a.Reason_Code GROUP BY r.Reason_Description, r.Reason_Category ORDER BY appeals DESC LIMIT 12
queries.rework: SELECT CASE WHEN Rework_Flag='Yes' THEN 'Reworked' ELSE 'Clean first pass' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM appeals_fact GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY avg_tat
queries.doc_gap: SELECT CASE WHEN Documentation_Complete='Yes' THEN 'Documentation complete at intake' ELSE 'Documentation incomplete at intake' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS appeals, ROUND(AVG(Intake_Days),2) AS intake_days, ROUND(AVG(Pending_Info_Days),2) AS pending_days, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat FROM appeals_fact GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY avg_tat
queries.priority: SELECT Priority, COUNT(*) AS appeals, MAX(SLA_Target_Days) AS target_days, ROUND(AVG(Turnaround_Days),1) AS avg_tat, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM appeals_fact GROUP BY Priority ORDER BY target_days DESC
queries.delay_reasons: SELECT COALESCE(r.Reason_Description, e.Delay_Reason) AS reason, COUNT(*) AS events FROM appeal_events e LEFT JOIN dim_reason_code r ON r.Reason_Code=e.Delay_Reason WHERE e.Delay_Reason IS NOT NULL AND e.Delay_Reason<>'' AND e.Delay_Reason<>'None' GROUP BY reason ORDER BY events DESC LIMIT 10
queries.stage_events: SELECT Process_Stage, COUNT(*) AS events, COUNT(DISTINCT Appeal_ID) AS appeals, ROUND(1.0*COUNT(*)/COUNT(DISTINCT Appeal_ID),2) AS events_per_appeal FROM appeal_events GROUP BY Process_Stage ORDER BY events DESC
queries.worst: SELECT Appeal_ID, Appeal_Type, Priority, Status, Turnaround_Days, Review_Wait_Days, Reassignment_Count, Friction_Category FROM appeals_fact WHERE Turnaround_Days IS NOT NULL ORDER BY Friction_Score DESC, Turnaround_Days DESC LIMIT 25
queries.exceptions: SELECT Rule_ID, Severity, Status, COUNT(*) AS exceptions FROM dq_exceptions GROUP BY Rule_ID, Severity, Status ORDER BY exceptions DESC

kpis.label: Avg turnaround
kpis.note: The average is not the problem

cards.title: Where the days actually go
cards.desc: Average days in each process stage. The single largest block is the queue between routing and the first clinical touch — time when nothing is happening and no team owns the appeal.

cards.title: Share of total turnaround
cards.desc: The same stages as a proportion of the 14.9-day average.

cards.title: Turnaround against the target, by appeal type
cards.desc: Each type carries its own SLA target. Average turnaround inside the target still produces a failing compliance rate, because compliance is decided by the tail rather than the mean.

cards.title: Friction bands behave the way the score says they should
cards.desc: Turnaround rises and compliance falls monotonically across the four bands. That is the strongest claim available for weights set by judgement rather than fitted to outcomes.

cards.title: The cost of an incomplete intake
cards.desc: Appeals arriving without complete documentation spend materially longer in pending-info status, and that wait lands inside the SLA clock rather than outside it.

cards.title: What rework costs
cards.desc: A reworked appeal takes substantially longer and is far less likely to meet SLA. Rework is measured by flag, not by reason code, so it cannot be split into avoidable and unavoidable here.

cards.title: Payer mix is not the explanation
cards.desc: Turnaround varies across payers, but not nearly enough to account for the compliance gap. Pending-info days track payer responsiveness more closely than internal handling time does.

cards.title: Monthly trend
cards.desc: Volume received against turnaround and compliance. Bars are appeals received on the right axis.

cards.title: Urgent triage is not actually urgent
cards.desc: Urgent appeals are held to a 7-day target and take 15.5 days — longer than the Standard queue's 14.8 against 30 days. The priority flag changes the target but not the handling, so compliance collapses to 16.5% on the flag that matters most.

cards.title: Logged delay reasons
cards.desc: Taken from the event log rather than the appeal record, so this counts occurrences of waiting, not appeals.

cards.title: Event volume by process stage
cards.desc: Events per appeal is a proxy for touch count. A stage with many events per appeal and few days elapsed is busy; one with few events and many days is a queue.

cards.title: Top reason codes
cards.desc: Volume, turnaround and overturn rate together. A high-volume code with a high overturn rate is a candidate for a pre-appeal fix rather than faster appeal handling.

cards.title: Highest-friction appeals
cards.desc: Ranked by Friction Score. Review wait is shown alongside to make a point: it is near zero on most of these, so the worst appeals are not the ones stuck waiting for a reviewer. They are the ones that were reworked, reassigned or held for information — which the stage averages above cannot surface.

cards.title: Data quality exception log
cards.desc: Every rule violation with its severity and current disposition. Blocking failures are excluded from reporting and logged, never silently corrected.
